name: 6 Wunderkinder
description: 6 Wunderkinder (6Wunderkinder GmbH) was a Berlin-based software startup founded in 2010 that built Wunderlist, a popular cross-platform to-do list and task management application. The company shipped a public REST API for Wunderlist in 2013, along with webhooks and integrations such as Slack and Sunrise, and rebuilt its backend into roughly 60 microservices behind a single unified API. Backed by Earlybird and Sequoia Capital, 6 Wunderkinder was acquired by Microsoft in June 2015 for a reported US$100-200M. Microsoft folded the product into Microsoft To Do and discontinued Wunderlist on 6 May 2020. This profile is retained as a historical record; the company is defunct and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation.

name: ablefy
description: ablefy (formerly elopage) is a German all-in-one sales and monetization platform for coaches, creators, trainers, consultants, and online educators. It provides conversion-optimized checkout with 12+ payment methods (PayPal, Klarna, SEPA, cards, Apple/Google Pay) across multiple currencies, an integrated LMS for online courses, memberships and subscriptions, community and live events, e-ticketing, automated invoicing with international tax/OSS compliance, and an optional reseller (merchant-of-record) model. Sellers can automate workflows through the ablefy API, webhooks, and access-token authentication, plus a Zapier integration and email-marketing connectors. The platform reports 80,000+ sellers, 6M+ customers serviced, and over EUR 2 billion in processed transactions across 13+ years of operation.

name: Afori
description: Afori is a Barcelona- and Germany-based insurtech building an AI software platform designed specifically for insurance brokers (Versicherungsmakler). Its first product is an AI Sidebar that lives inside Microsoft Outlook and broker management systems (Maklerverwaltungsprogramme), turning unstructured emails and documents into structured, review-ready cases with tasks and reminders, context-aware email drafts, and prefilled claim notifications. Specialized AI agents (KI-Helfer) automate insurance-specific back-office work while keeping every action documented and auditable. The platform is EU-hosted, GDPR (DSGVO) compliant, ISO 27001:2022 certified, and built within the European regulatory framework (IDD, EU AI Act). Founded in 2025 by former wefox leaders Fabian Wesemann (CEO) and Sergi Banos (CTO), Afori raised a EUR 4M round led by General Catalyst. This API Evangelist profile was created as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched from Afori's public web surface; the company currently publishes no developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI.

name: Agile Robots
description: Agile Robots SE is a Munich-based robotics and artificial intelligence company founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics. The company develops force-sensitive industrial and service robots, robotic arms (Diana series), grippers and hands (Agile Hand), mobile robotics, and the AgileCore / AgileAI software platform that lets system integrators and operators build and deploy AI-driven automation for the automotive, consumer electronics, healthcare, and service industries. Headquartered in Munich's Sendling district with manufacturing across Europe, China, and India, Agile Robots reached unicorn valuation in a 2021 Series C and is backed by investors including Hongshan (Sequoia Capital China). This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Agile Robots does not currently publish a public developer portal, REST API, or first-party SDKs.

name: Aleph Alpha2
description: Aleph Alpha is a Heidelberg, Germany-based artificial intelligence company building sovereign, specialized large language models (SLLMs) for European enterprises and public-sector organizations operating in regulated and sensitive domains. Its PhariaAI suite is an end-to-end, self-hostable stack — PhariaStudio for building AI applications, PhariaAssistant for knowledge workers, and PhariaOS for resource management, alongside the PhariaInference, PhariaSearch, and PhariaData APIs — engineered for data sovereignty, transparency, and EU regulatory compliance while running on European infrastructure. The PhariaInference HTTP API exposes text completion, chat, embeddings, semantic search, tokenization, and explainability, accessed with a bearer token issued from app.aleph-alpha.com and supported by an official open-source Python client.

name: Amperecloud
description: Amperecloud (Amperecloud GmbH) is a German renewable-energy management software company whose cloud platform provides an operating system for monitoring, operating, and commercially managing solar, wind, and other renewable-energy assets at scale. The platform brings asset performance monitoring, maintenance and ticket management, commercial and technical asset management, and virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities into a single system, supported by migration, consulting, and custom-integration services. It is used by more than 300 customers worldwide managing over 8,000 installations and 10+ GWp of capacity. Added to the API Evangelist network as a point-nine portfolio company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published, so this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe pending any future public API surface.

name: Audi Connect / myAudi
description: Audi Connect is the connected-vehicle services platform from Audi AG, the Ingolstadt, Germany-based luxury automaker and member of the Volkswagen Group. Delivered to drivers through the embedded MMI infotainment system and the myAudi companion app for iOS and Android, Audi Connect spans remote vehicle control (lock/unlock, remote start, climate pre-conditioning, EV charge management), safety and security (Emergency Call/eCall, Audi Service Request, stolen-vehicle locator, geofencing, speed alerts), and in-car infotainment (real-time traffic, satellite map imagery, parking and fuel information, weather, news, natural voice recognition, Amazon Alexa, Amazon Music, Wi-Fi hotspot, and an in-vehicle app store with Disney+ and passenger gaming on supported models). Services are packaged as Audi connect CARE (included for ten years on new U.S. Audis), Audi connect NAV (navigation and live traffic), and Audi connect PLUS (premium streaming and Wi-Fi). For EVs and PHEVs, Audi Connect adds charging-station search, remote charge monitoring, and cabin pre-conditioning. Audi does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, OAuth program, or partner SDK for myAudi/Audi Connect; programmatic access today is brokered by third-party connected-car aggregators (Smartcar, High Mobility, Enode, Mojio) under Audi's commercial agreements, and community projects reverse-engineer the mobile-app endpoints. Audi has publicly discussed an internal OpenAPI-driven API management strategy (with Nagarro) but the surface remains private to Audi, VW Group brands, and authorized partners.

name: avimedical
description: Avi Medical is a technology-enabled primary care provider headquartered in Munich, Germany, operating a network of modern general-practice (Hausarzt) medical practices paired with a patient-facing mobile app for booking appointments, video consultations, prescriptions, and digital access to medical records. The company combines physical clinics with digital health tooling to modernize German primary care, and is backed by Balderton Capital among other investors. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal has been found on its public surface as of this enrichment pass.

name: aWATTar
description: aWATTar provides a free, public REST API delivering real-time and next-day hourly electricity spot prices sourced from the EPEX Spot market exchange for both Austria and Germany. The API enables developers, smart home integrators, and commercial operators to build dynamic energy pricing applications that respond to market conditions. Prices are updated daily at 14:00 CET covering the following day, and the API returns JSON data including start/end timestamps and market price per MWh. No authentication token is required, making integration straightforward for any developer. The service is offered free of charge under a fair-use policy of 100 requests per day per client, supporting use cases such as EV charging optimization, smart heating control, and automated energy management systems.

name: Billie
description: Billie is a Berlin-based B2B "buy now, pay later" (BNPL) payment provider that lets merchants offer business buyers invoice purchase, pay-after-delivery, and installment terms at checkout while Billie assumes the credit and fraud risk and pays the merchant out. Its Payment API v2 (paella.billie.io) uses OAuth 2.0 client-credentials and covers checkout sessions, a hosted payment page, direct backend order creation, order management, captures (invoicing), payment confirmation, refunds/credit notes, and a webhook event surface. Billie also ships an embeddable checkout widget, a PHP SDK, e-commerce plugins (Shopware, Magento, WooCommerce, JTL), and partner routes via Klarna, Mollie, Adyen, Stripe, and Kustom. Backed by Creandum and Speedinvest.

name: Candis
description: Candis is a Berlin-based fintech (founded 2015) offering an AI-driven financial process automation and accounts-payable platform for SMEs. It captures incoming invoices, reads invoice data via OCR (business partner, amount, date, IBAN), routes them through approval workflows, and exports approved postings to accounting systems and ERPs. As a licensed DATEV interface partner it also integrates with Sage and Wolters Kluwer, and supports three-way matching of invoices against purchase orders and goods receipts. Candis exposes a public REST API (developer.candis.io) with an Export API, Core Data API, and read-only Invoice, Reimbursement Item, and Purchase Request Data APIs, secured with OAuth2/OIDC and fronted by an official MCP server.

name: Causa Prima
description: Causa Prima is an AI-native fintech building an agent-to-agent network for finance teams — automating invoicing, dispute resolution, and dynamic (early-payment) discounting between buyers and suppliers. Its first public product, Scribo, is a free, EN 16931-compliant e-invoicing engine that generates German ZUGFeRD and XRechnung, plus plain US PDF invoices, through five surfaces: a web UI, an HTTP API, a hosted MCP server, an npm CLI, and a Claude / ChatGPT / Codex Agent Skill — all backed by the same public /api/v1 API with no signup (the sender's email is the login via a magic link). The team previously built Taulia (acquired by SAP) and Finoa; Causa Prima is backed by Creandum.

name: Caya
description: Caya (Caya GmbH, Berlin) is a German intelligent document processing (IDP) company whose Document Automation Suite digitizes, classifies, and routes business documents end to end. Its core capabilities are Post Scan (physical mail intake with OCR and automatic classification), Document Extractions (AI-powered structured data extraction), and Document Automations (rule-based routing and distribution into downstream systems). Caya connects to 100+ tools across accounting, ERP, HR, cloud storage, and e-signature, and hosts data in a high-security Frankfurt data center. It is certified and compliant against ISO 27001, GDPR/DSGVO, DORA, GoBD, and German HGB/AO retention rules, with a public Vanta-hosted trust center. Surfaced as an HV Capital portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

name: CERPRO
description: CERPRO is a Berlin-based industrial software company building AI-powered quality-assurance and process automation for small and medium-sized manufacturers. Its flagship product, QualiSpec, uses computer-vision and large-model AI to automatically extract features, dimensions, tolerances and drill-hole specifications from technical drawings (PDF, JPG, DXF) and generate inspection reports and quality documents in customized templates such as VDA, EMPB and inspection plans. This removes manual copy-paste and data-entry work from quality control, cutting documentation time by up to 70-90% and reducing errors while creating a unified data foundation that connects OEMs and suppliers. Since launching in December 2024 the software has been adopted by more than 100 SMEs across aerospace, medical devices and mechanical engineering. CERPRO is a Techstars portfolio company and raised a ~EUR 2M pre-seed round in 2025. The product is delivered as a cloud SaaS platform (platform.cerpro.io) hosted on AWS in Germany, with an ISO 27001 certified, GDPR/BDSG-compliant data-security posture.

name: Check24
description: "CHECK24 is Germany's largest online comparison portal (Vergleichsportal), founded in 1999 and headquartered in Munich. It lets more than 20 million customers compare prices and switch providers across over 50 categories, including car, life and health insurance, loans and bank accounts, electricity and gas, DSL and mobile tariffs, travel, rental cars, and online shopping. CHECK24 runs its own comparison calculators and a licensed bank (CHECK24 Bank), and integrates partner providers such as Allianz Direct through API-based connections. Backed by Accel, it is profiled in the API Evangelist network as a consumer company. CHECK24 maintains a verified GitHub organization and a GenDev developer scholarship program but publishes no public developer API."

name: Chemtura
description: Chemtura Corporation was a global specialty chemicals company that developed, manufactured, and marketed chemical intermediates, additives, specialty chemicals, urethanes, organometallics, and modern plastics. In April 2017, Chemtura was acquired by LANXESS AG, the German specialty chemicals company headquartered in Cologne, and its operations were integrated into LANXESS's Performance Materials and other business segments. Chemtura products are now marketed and supported through LANXESS, which continues to serve agriculture, animal care, mobility, consumer goods, electrical and electronics, energy, food, and healthcare end markets.

name: Clark
description: Clark ("Dein Versicherungsmanager") is a Germany-based digital insurance manager that lets consumers view, compare, optimize, and manage all of their insurance policies in one mobile app and web platform. Founded in Frankfurt in 2015, Clark pairs a licensed insurance brokerage with automated tariff comparison across more than 180 insurance providers and free expert consultation, covering health, liability, property, life, mobility, and retirement products. The company operates across Germany, Switzerland, France, and the UK, serves over 700,000 customers, and is backed by venture investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Clark exposes no public developer API or developer portal; it is a consumer-facing insurtech rather than an API producer.

name: CNC24
description: CNC24 is a German online manufacturing platform for ordering custom CNC parts and precision components. Customers upload CAD files (STEP, STP, DWG, DXF, PDF and 3D data) and receive a binding quote within 48 hours, with production routed through a vetted network of 500+ manufacturers across 21 countries and roughly 5,500 machines. An AI-powered matching algorithm assigns each request to partners with the right expertise and production environment. Supported processes include CNC milling, turning, laser and waterjet cutting, sheet metal bending, punching, EDM, 3D printing, injection molding and die casting, serving aerospace, automotive, medical, robotics, construction and energy customers. The platform runs a fully digital workflow from quoting to delivery with order tracking, ISO 9001:2015 quality assurance, AES-256 encryption and anonymized drawings shared with partners. CNC24 is a Seedcamp portfolio company. No public developer API, SDKs or API documentation are published.

name: Complori
description: Complori is a Berlin, Germany based online education company that teaches children and young people to code through live, small-group video classes led by qualified coaches in a protected digital space. Its programs span programming with Minecraft, Python, JavaScript game development, app development, and financial literacy, backed by a learning platform with challenges and exercises, a mobile learning app, completion certificates, flexible family-friendly scheduling, and holiday camps. Complori operates a B2C consumer education service (with parents as the decision-makers) rather than a developer-facing API product, and runs an education scholarship program to broaden access across socioeconomic backgrounds. Backed by Speedinvest.

name: conrizon
description: conrizon AG is a German holding company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in Essen, that unites four of Europe's leading Enterprise Content Management (ECM) brands - easy software, PROXESS, HABEL, and Portal Systems (Shareflex), alongside the friendWorks professional-services unit - under one roof. The group provides legally compliant, audit-proof digital archiving (GDPR, GoBD, eIDAS), document management (DMS), invoice and procure-to-pay (P2P) processing, contract management, and HR/HCM software with automated workflows, plus AI services and connectors for SAP and Microsoft 365 / SharePoint. Solutions are offered cloud-native, in a private cloud, on-premises, or hybrid, and are relied on by more than 8,700 companies and organizations worldwide. conrizon is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer API or developer portal.

name: CrossEngage
description: CrossEngage is a Berlin-based customer data and cross-channel marketing platform (a Customer Data Platform / CDP) founded in 2015 and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital. It unifies first-party customer data into 360-degree profiles, builds no-code predictive AI/ML models for customer lifetime value and behavior, manages audiences with drag-and-drop segmentation, and orchestrates real-time cross-channel customer journeys. Following its acquisition by Spotler, the product is offered as Spotler Activate Pro. CrossEngage exposes a REST API at api.crossengage.io documented at api.documentation.crossengage.io, covering User Management (v1.0 and v2.0), Product Feed, File Attachments, Export, and Statistics.

name: Cylib
description: Cylib is a German battery recycling company founded in 2022 as a spinoff from RWTH Aachen University, headquartered in Aachen, Germany. It transforms end-of-life lithium-ion batteries, production scrap, and black mass back into critical raw materials, recovering lithium, graphite, nickel, cobalt, and manganese through a proprietary, largely water-based hydrometallurgical process that the company reports achieves over 90% recycling efficiency with an ~80% reduced carbon footprint versus primary extraction, powered by 100% renewable electricity. The company is backed by Speedinvest and other investors. Cylib operates as an industrial cleantech / circular-economy materials business and does not currently publish a developer program, public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other software integration surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and carries only identity and public web properties.

Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

name: DCS-Touristik (DCS Travel)
description: DCS-Touristik GmbH, trading as DCS Travel (dcs.travel), is a German river- and sea-cruise operator based in Nagel, Germany. The company organizes river cruises on major European waterways — primarily the Danube and the Rhine — as well as sea cruises along the Croatian coast, operating its own vessels including the DCS Amethyst 1 and DCS Amethyst 2. Its business is direct consumer travel booking: multi-day cruise packages (roughly 3 to 12 days), organized transfers and shore excursions, themed sailings, travel-insurance partnerships, and early-booking discounts. This is a consumer-facing tourism brand with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer documentation. It was originally added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio stub; that classification appears to be a false match (the "early-bird" cruise discount wording rather than the Earlybird venture firm), and no API surface was found during enrichment.

name: dehaze
description: dehaze is a Munich-area (Fürstenfeldbruck, Germany) healthtech company, part of the Techstars Berlin cohort, building proprietary causal AI infrastructure that detects chronic and autoimmune disease earlier by identifying overlooked diagnoses, health risks, and inappropriate treatments. Its platform unifies and harmonizes diverse health data (lab results, medical imaging, genomics, clinical notes) into doctor-validated patient journeys, risk-profiles individuals against millions of health journeys and medical guidelines, and runs targeted AI follow-ups to improve treatment adherence for patients, payers, and providers. dehaze has analyzed over 250,000 patient lives across 300 million health events and 200+ AI algorithms, and raised €3.2M in 2026. dehaze publishes no first-party developer API; it exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint and an llms.txt for agentic AI access to public site content.

name: digitaleseiten
description: Digitale Seiten is a German online marketing company that operates a network of 28+ industry-specific business directories for craftspeople and local service providers (for example Elektriker.org, Klempner.org, Maler.org and Dachdecker.org). The platform lets tradespeople create free business listings, distributes regional customer inquiries and job requests to registered companies as leads, improves their search-engine visibility, and provides review-collection tools. According to the company it lists 869,000+ registered businesses and has matched 765,000+ job assignments. It is a B2B directory and lead-generation service and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. Backed by Point Nine.

name: Doctorly
description: Doctorly (doctorly GmbH, Berlin) builds a modern cloud-based practice management system (Praxisverwaltungssystem / PVS) for medical practices in Germany, positioned as a replacement for legacy systems such as Medistar, Turbomed and ALBIS. The platform covers KV quarterly billing, e-prescription (eRezept), electronic sick leave (eAU), real-time collaborative patient records, GDT device integration and cross-platform access on Windows, macOS, Linux and Android, and it is KBV-, gematik- and GDPR-compliant. Doctorly is a Seedcamp portfolio company. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/FHIR specification, SDKs or GitHub organization; this entry is maintained as a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network.

name: Donnerstag Ai
description: Donnerstag.ai (Donnerstag.ai Technologies GmbH) is a Frankfurt-based enterprise fintech building an AI Reconciliation Layer for enterprise finance. Its platform automates financial reconciliation at the line-item level across accounts payable, accounts receivable, bank, and intercompany flows, adapting to each customer's systems, data sources, workflows, and roles. The stated goal is 100% line-item coverage at T+0 so the financial close becomes a confirmation rather than a month-end scramble, with an immutable audit trail for GoBD, IFRS, SOX, and BEPS. The company serves logistics, payment service providers, retail and e-commerce, manufacturing, human resources, and construction, is EU-hosted in Frankfurt, and is founded by Barbaros Ozbugutu and Volkan Ozkan and backed by Speedinvest. As a solution-and-services provider it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or docs.

name: element 5 AG
description: element 5 AG was a German e-commerce and digital-distribution company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Cologne, Germany. It operated a platform that let software developers and publishers sell their products and licenses directly to customers online, growing to more than 10,000 clients across 150 countries and becoming one of Europe's leading software e-commerce providers. element 5 was acquired by U.S.-based Digital River (its direct competitor) for roughly $120M and subsequently absorbed and renamed Digital River GmbH, ceasing to operate as an independent company. It was an early Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company; this profile records its identity and exit. No live independent API or developer surface remains to enrich.

name: Eleqtron
description: eleQtron GmbH is a German quantum computing hardware company founded in 2020 as a spin-off from the Quantum Optics Department at the University of Siegen by Prof. Dr. Christof Wunderlich, Dr. Michael Johanning (CTO), and Jan Leisse (CEO). Based in Siegen, Germany, eleQtron develops freely programmable, scalable trapped-ion quantum computers built on its proprietary MAGIC (Magnetic Gradient Induced Coupling) technology, which controls qubits with microwaves rather than lasers for higher precision and a clearer path to scaling. The company aims to become a leading provider of quantum computing time for industrial applications across chemicals, pharmaceuticals, automotive, logistics, finance, and machine learning. eleQtron's systems are made accessible to developers through cloud platforms and standard quantum frameworks (Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane) rather than a first-party public REST API. Backed by Earlybird Venture Capital.

name: Encentive
description: encentive GmbH is a German industrial energy-technology company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Neumuenster. Its AI-driven smart energy management platform, flexOn, automatically optimizes and controls electricity consumption for industrial and commercial operations, orchestrating assets such as PV/solar systems, battery storage, heat pumps, cooling and thermal storage, CHP, wind, and EV charging infrastructure alongside existing energy management systems. flexOn combines plant data, weather forecasts, and real-time market prices to shift loads to periods when energy is cheapest and greenest, cutting energy costs by up to 20% and CO2 emissions by up to 30%. It integrates with industrial assets over REST API, SFTP, OPC UA, and Modbus TCP. encentive publishes no public developer API, portal, or specification; integration is delivered as part of its managed platform, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

description: ExpressSteuer (formerly Express Group) is a German tax-technology company, originally a Hamburg-based fintech backed by Insight Partners that offered an app-based, largely automated income-tax-return (Steuererklärung) service aimed at consumers and employees. The expresssteuer.de domain currently presents a German-language tax-information and guidance website (built on WordPress) covering income tax, self-employment, and everyday financial topics. No public developer program, API, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface is published. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead for enrichment.

name: Felmo
description: felmo (felmo GmbH) is a mobile veterinary practice (mobile Tierarztpraxis) headquartered in Berlin, Germany that brings licensed veterinarians directly to pet owners' homes for dogs and cats. Founded in 2019 by CEO Philip Trockels, felmo operates across Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Düsseldorf and 25+ additional German cities, and has treated 300,000+ animals with 8,000+ home visits per month via 140+ mobile vets. Services include preventive care and consultations, examinations and diagnostics, laboratory and imaging, surgical procedures (including a fully-equipped mobile operating vehicle / OP-Wagen), dental medicine and holistic pet care, billed per the German veterinary fee schedule (GOT). Customers book appointments, access medical records and lab results, receive reminders, and message support through the felmo iOS and Android app. felmo is backed by HV Capital and additional venture investors. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public identity and web properties.

name: Fidor Bank
description: Fidor Bank was a German digital challenger bank founded in Munich in 2009 and an early pioneer of Banking-as-a-Service and open banking through its fidorOS / bankOS middleware platform and public REST API, which covered Customers, Accounts, Transfers, Transactions and Account Information over an OAuth2 authorization-code flow. Fidor was acquired by France's Groupe BPCE in 2016; following years of post-acquisition integration struggles the bank ceased business operations in mid-2023 and entered liquidation. Its developer portal (fidor.com) is now a parked domain and the sandbox and production API hosts are offline. The surviving first-party developer artifacts are the archived official Ruby client (RubyGems: fidor_api, by Fidor Solutions AG) and the github.com/fidor organization. This is a retired provider retained for historical reference.

name: Fincompare
description: Fincompare (now operating under the Fynbiz brand alongside Compeon) is a Berlin-based digital financing marketplace for small and medium-sized enterprises. Founded in 2017, the platform lets businesses request, compare, and close financing offers from 100+ banks and alternative lenders in one place, covering business loans, leasing, factoring, goods and warehouse financing, real-estate financing, and revenue-based financing. Fincompare connects lenders such as ING, VR Smart Finanz, and iwoca directly through bank API integrations to automate credit decisions. The company was acquired by a consortium of DZ Bank, several Volksbanken, and Atruvia in 2021. Fincompare operates a customer-facing SME financing product; it does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface.

name: Finiata
description: Finiata was a Berlin-founded fintech providing working-capital and invoice financing to small businesses, freelancers and micro-enterprises, operating principally in Germany and Poland and backed by investors including Point Nine. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass Finiata has no live public surface: finiata.com is registered but fully undelegated (no NS, SOA, A, MX or TXT records) and does not resolve; the former developer portal developer.finiata.com, archived as live in 2019, no longer resolves; and finiata.de has been taken over by unrelated third-party gambling-affiliate content. The only live first-party assets found are the company's GitHub organization (github.com/debitech) and one unmaintained internal npm tooling package. No API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, documentation, or well-known surface exists to catalog.

name: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg
description: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU) is a public research university in Bavaria, Germany, ranked #224 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. FAU does not operate a single consolidated developer portal, but several of its central services expose public, machine-readable interfaces. The University Library's OPEN FAU institutional repository runs on DSpace 7.4 and publishes a browsable REST/HAL API and an OAI-PMH metadata interface, while the FAU CRIS research information system (built on Clarivate Converis) exposes a public web-service path that is access-restricted on FAU's instance. Central IT (RRZE) and the Competence Center for Research Data and Information (CDI) maintain active public GitHub organizations and a self-hosted GitLab.

name: Getsafe

It serves 500k+ customers in Germany and Austria with English-language, app-based support. name: HV Capital
description: HV Capital is one of Europe's leading early-stage and growth venture capital firms, headquartered in Munich with an office in Berlin. Founded in 2000 as Holtzbrinck Ventures (the venture arm associated with Verlagsgruppe Georg von Holtzbrinck), the partnership completed a management buyout and rebranded to HV Capital in 2018, establishing full operational and investment independence. The firm backs European founders with global ambitions across the full lifecycle: its Venture fund writes seed and Series A checks from roughly €500K to €10M, while its Growth fund invests through Series B and beyond with checks up to €60M and follow-on reserves reaching €100M per company. The firm reports more than €2.8B in assets under management across nine fund generations spanning Venture and Growth, over 290 portfolio companies, and 12 IPOs. Its investment philosophy — "too new is our baseline, too bold is our reason, too complex is our edge" — reflects a willingness to back complex, category-defining companies. Founded in 2016, Inuru operates the automated "Dragon Factory" OLED production line in Wildau and works with brands such as Coca-Cola and Marvel on interactive, sustainable smart-packaging and medication-adherence labels. Its "Talent.KI" product applies artificial intelligence to candidate sourcing and regional labor-market analysis, surfacing employers where job seekers actually search. name: KUKA
description: KUKA AG is a German industrial automation company headquartered in Augsburg, Bavaria, founded in 1898 and majority-owned by China's Midea Group since 2016. KUKA designs and manufactures industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), production cells, controllers, and the software stack that drives them. Its product portfolio spans six-axis articulated robots (KR series), sensitive collaborative robots (LBR iiwa, LBR iisy), mobile platforms (KMR iiwa, KMP), and palletizing/welding/CNC cells, controlled by the KR C4 and KR C5 / KR C5 micro controller generations. The robot software stack centers on KUKA System Software (KSS/VSS) for KR C4-class hardware, the newer iiQKA.OS / iiQKA.OS2 operating system for KR C5, and the KUKA Robot Language (KRL) for motion programming, with extension surfaces including KUKA.RobotSensorInterface (RSI), KUKA.EthernetKRL, KUKA.PLC mxAutomation for external PLC control, KUKA.OPC UA, and KUKA.AppTech / iiQKA App Builder for option packages. Engineering and simulation are delivered through iiQWorks (iiQWorks.Sim, iiQWorks.App Builder, iiQWorks.Copilot) and KUKA.Sim, while operational software includes KUKA Xpert (documentation/cloud), KUKA iiQoT (condition monitoring), and KUKA Connect / my.KUKA customer portals. KUKA does not publish a first-party public REST/OpenAPI developer API or an official GitHub organization for its robot control stack; integration is performed through proprietary protocols (RSI, EthernetKRL, mxAutomation, OPC UA, PROFINET, EtherCAT) and SDKs distributed via the iiQKA Creator portal and KUKA Xpert. A meaningful body of open-source KUKA integration code lives in the community-maintained kroshu GitHub organization (ROS 2 drivers, external-control SDK, URDF robot descriptions) and the roboticsapi / openkuka projects. KUKA serves automotive, electronics, battery, metal, consumer goods, healthcare, aerospace, and e-commerce logistics customers, and through its Swisslog subsidiary extends into warehouse and intralogistics automation.

The platform helps practices participate in clinical trials via automated indication screening and patient recruitment, giving physicians time back while opening a research revenue stream. description: Point Nine Capital is a thesis-driven, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in Berlin, Germany. description: Polyteia is a Berlin-based govtech company offering a data platform for the German and European public sector. The platform is fully driveable through an RPC-style API (command/query over a single POST endpoint) authenticated with Personal Access Keys, backed by a Trust Center and GDPR/BSI/C5 compliance. Founded by Faruk Tuncer, Taisia Antonova, and Lukas Rambold; backed by HV Capital and DvH Ventures.

PowerUs reports 250,000+ registered skilled workers and 6,000+ open positions. It is a consumer/employer marketplace product and does not currently expose a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI-described API surface; its api.powerus.de and docs.powerus.de hosts are private/internal (docs gated behind Cloudflare Access).
